# mcloud kubeconfig

<!-- Generated by `go run ./internal/gendocs`: edit the source it names, not this file. -->

_Generated from the command's help in `internal/cli`._

[All commands](README.md)

Write the kubeconfig that logs in through Authelia (mcloud login does this).

Write a kubeconfig for the cluster whose user is you through Authelia:
kubectl and mcloud run mcloud credential for a token, which logs in when
needed. mcloud login writes it by itself; this writes it again, e.g.
somewhere else for kubectl.

The cluster's address and CA come from the platform's discovery document
(https://maxcloud.gronblom.dev/.well-known/maxcloud.json), else from your current kubeconfig.

mcloud uses it unless --kubeconfig or $MCLOUD\_KUBECONFIG say otherwise.
For kubectl: set -gx KUBECONFIG &lt;file&gt;.

```
mcloud kubeconfig [flags]
```

Examples:

```fish
mcloud kubeconfig
mcloud kubeconfig --out ~/.kube/homelab-oidc.yaml
```

Flags:

| Flag | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--client-id` string | `kubernetes` | its client for the cluster, the API server's audience ($MCLOUD\_OIDC\_CLIENT\_ID) |
| `--issuer` string | `https://auth.lab.gronblom.dev` | OpenID Connect provider the cluster trusts ($MCLOUD\_OIDC\_ISSUER) |
| `--name` string | `homelab` | cluster and context name in it |
| `--out` string | `~/.config/mcloud/kubeconfig` | where to write it |
